I could not verify this against the source literature, so the answer below is a reasoned guess rather than a derived result.

**Setup.** For $p$ odd, $\text{Aut}(\mathbb{Z}_{p^n})\cong \mathbb{Z}_{p^{n-1}(p-1)}$ is cyclic. It has exactly one subgroup of each order $d$ dividing $p^{n-1}(p-1)$.

**Guess for the three subgroups.** I assumed the three subgroups are the "natural" ones:
- the $p'$-part, of order $p-1$;
- the Sylow $p$-subgroup, of order $p^{n-1}$;
- the whole group $\text{Aut}(G)$, of order $p^{n-1}(p-1)$.

**Sum of distinct orders.**
$$
(p-1) + p^{n-1} + p^{n-1}(p-1) = (p-1) + p^{n-1}\cdot p = p^n + p - 1.
$$

This rests on the assumed identification of the three subgroups, which I did not check against the theorem.

ANSWER: $p^n + p - 1$
